scope: Focused local follow-up after user-reported platform static45/45 and rubric52/53; unchanged-source review retained, shared authentication gate reassessed. Not a fresh platform verdict.

items.description: The prompt reads like a real person asking for an app, not a spec sheet, checklist, or build recipe.
items.assessment: Root brief is a product request; technical details are in five short subject files.

items.description: Keeps an authentic human voice (casual/terse is good); not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated prose.
items.assessment: New guarantees are explicit product requirements in ballots.md and privacy.md. No target score, hidden field name or benchmark instruction enters the brief.

items.description: No real spelling errors and nothing pasted in by mistake (author notes, TODOs, stray paths, contradictions).
items.assessment: No other-product names in delivered prompts, author TODOs or host paths found.

items.description: Everything the judges grade is asked for, and the runtime contract (path, start command, port, storage, seed, accounts, no-network) is stated.
items.assessment: Existing runtime contract unchanged. Original status/body receipts and viewed roster revisions now explicitly support the new assertions.

items.description: The prompt never names the judge, rubric, dimensions, weights, test paths, or grader sentinels.
items.assessment: Builder instructions contain no test paths, rubric weights or judge identifiers.

items.description: One reasonable reading, and every capability is reachable from the seed + runtime with no network. Reports every ambiguity/unreachable item.
items.assessment: Both images build; exact four-account seed is reachable; golden workflows run offline locally.

items.description: Real build work is required; a stub or trivial tweak can't earn the reward.
items.assessment: Authenticated ballot product with anonymous choices, lifecycle, durable success/refusal receipts and competing roster snapshots.

items.description: Name, directory slug, description, keywords, and metadata all describe THIS task and agree.
items.assessment: Task name turing/common-ground-ballot, wrapper and task-specific metadata agree; version is 1.0.0.

items.description: Agent image is no-network with sane CPU/memory, no secret literals, and nothing that secretly needs an install.
items.assessment: Explicit current lead override: public agent network; exact reference CPU/memory/env, no secret literals.

items.description: Verifier runs separately on a pinned image + allowlist, with the judge model and API key fully wired.
items.assessment: Separate verifier and exact reference provider/model settings; real credential invocation not run locally.

items.description: Agent, verifier, liveness, and judge timeouts are long enough and nest properly (inner < outer, sum of judges < verifier).
items.assessment: Reference 12000-second judge sum <12600 wrapper <13200 verifier. Final full LLM timing remains untested.

items.description: [environment].docker_image isn't set while the agent Dockerfile still has active build steps (which would skip it entirely).
items.assessment: No prebuilt agent image override; Dockerfile is built.

items.description: Any shipped inputs exist at the expected path and match what the prompt, solution, and judges assume (or N/A if none needed).
items.assessment: Seed copies match byte-for-byte; documented instructions and seed paths exist in agent image.

items.description: Shipped data is self-consistent, synthetic (no real PII), and free of orphan references or injection payloads.
items.assessment: Four synthetic accounts, ballot choice/eligibility/participation references validated; no injected probe fixture.

items.description: Agent image is pinned, pre-installs every runtime dependency (no run-time install), and stages the assets.
items.assessment: Reference base tags retained and resolved image IDs recorded; Express5.1.0 and native SQLite12.4.1 smoke pass.

items.description: The agent's world has the inputs and the ask, but no finished copy of the deliverable.
items.assessment: Agent image contains instructions/seed, no /tests and no completed /app/server.js.

items.description: The reference plausibly implements every feature/screen the instruction asks for.
items.assessment: Golden source is unchanged. All 32 local browser groups pass, including the original 27 workflows and five complete authentication gates after two restarts.

items.description: The reference plausibly satisfies every criterion the judges score, so the oracle can score high.
items.assessment: Updated gates pass in every dimension on the golden app. Original behavior, screenshots and contrast checks still pass locally; a new Oracle/Visual score is unmeasured.

items.description: solve.sh installs to the expected paths and the reference runs under the stated contract with no network / no run-time install.
items.assessment: Golden solve.sh installs into /app and runs with network disabled in local verification.

items.description: The reference is a committed, static baseline - not regenerated, fetched, or nondeterministic on any pinned value.
items.assessment: Golden source and archive SHA256 frozen; dynamic ids/timestamps are not pinned score values.

items.description: test.sh launches the app safely, gates on liveness, and writes a reward on every code path (including failures).
items.assessment: 15 local runner cases exercise score validation, zero gates, missing entry, HTTP500, delayed readiness and link boundaries.

items.description: The verifier Dockerfile ships a pinned browser, Playwright, judge CLI, rewardkit, and the runtime to start the app.
items.assessment: Exact updated verifier image builds; real RewardKit discovers36 criteria; central Codex max config loads.

items.description: Every launch assumption in test.sh (probe URL, env vars, paths, seed, deps, same-origin) was told to the agent. Signature check of this format.
items.assessment: Runtime paths, DB_PATH, seed, health, user roles and launch contract agree with instructions.

items.description: reward.toml and every judge.toml are structurally complete: pinned judge, browser MCP server, well-typed criteria with weights, valid aggregate.
items.assessment: All 115 reference-configuration checks pass. Another 55 focused wording checks validate the gate itself, not unrelated criterion text elsewhere in the prompt.

items.description: Every dimension prompt sends the judge into the live app via the browser tool - not scoring from source, memory, or first paint.
items.assessment: All5 prompts name live local browser evaluation; SQL is limited to the documented read-only Constraints inspection.

items.description: Every requirement the prompt states maps to at least one criterion (nothing asked-for goes ungraded). Reports every gap.
items.assessment: Unchanged criterion coverage map retained; explicit global-gate mappings added for documented passwords, signed-in identity and protected session-bound data.

items.description: No criterion enforces something the prompt/professional default never required (no false-fail on correct apps). Reports every instance.
items.assessment: No new product behavior, API name or mandatory extra status convention was introduced. Wrong password uses the existing seeded account; access refusal must not leak private records. Legitimate public demo hints remain allowed.

items.description: No two criteria grade the same thing twice, subsume each other, or demand incompatible products.
items.assessment: Criterion IDs, descriptions and weights are unchanged. Authentication is an explicit shared prerequisite with no extra reward mass; other failures remain independently scored.

items.description: Every dimension carries the browser gate that hard-zeros blank/static-shell/cross-origin apps (plus auth/backing checks when relevant).
items.assessment: All five gates now require public sign-in, wrong-password refusal, positive login/identity/backend/refresh and fresh-context denial of protected reads before and after a wrong login. A permissive password or public private-data endpoint zeros the entire dimension.

items.description: Any 'rejects / hides / absent' check is paired with the matching success case, so a totally broken app can't earn it.
items.assessment: Nine deliberately broken variants detected. New permissive-password, public-collection and leaking-denial variants each fail the corresponding gate assertion in all five dimensions.

items.description: 'Every / all / only / exactly-one' criteria require the whole collection, and 'unchanged' guards don't punish legit side-effects. Reports every instance.
items.assessment: Current whole-state snapshots remain unchanged after each exact replay/refusal. Saved receipts and roster visibility are verified after each of two actual restarts.

items.description: Each criterion is a concrete, browser-observable outcome with durable evidence and distinctive probes. Reports every instance.
items.assessment: Normal staff actions use real UI. Captured requests supply actual operation transport and revisions; read-only protected rereads verify current state. No new fixed schema or selector is imposed.

items.description: Each criterion states ONE full-credit bar - it doesn't enumerate several things then waive most, leaving the judge two targets. Reports every instance.
items.assessment: Each binary criterion retains all observations; UI prevention is a legitimate negative control, not an unattempted invalid submission.

items.description: If interactive/animated/responsive/themed, the judges actually click, wait, resize, or toggle - not score a still first paint.
items.assessment: Real keyboard/modal/theme/mobile/reduced-motion interactions tested; settled screenshots inspected.

items.description: At least one criterion proves the defining behavior works, and (where stateful) state survives reload/re-auth and is server-backed where required.
items.assessment: Original staff receipts, refusal receipts, roster snapshots, sessions and results pass both actual restarts. Added gate checks preserve all current domain records.

items.description: Distinctive values the judge creates to prove a mutation aren't already in the seed or the reference's initial state.
items.assessment: All new named fixtures are absent from the authoritative seed and are created through visible controls.

items.description: A later dimension doesn't assume a pristine seed after an earlier dimension mutated the shared running app.
items.assessment: Gate uses current records after earlier mutations and new browser contexts, not reseeding, global session revocation or a requirement for original seed counts.

items.description: Batched dimension prompts tell the judge to score each criterion on its own and continue after a failure (one miss can't zero the rest).
items.assessment: Explicit independent criterion scoring in all5 prompts; incomplete evidence is disclosed, never invented as an app failure.

items.description: A blank / static / mock / seed-copy / keyword-stuffed / refusing submission scores near zero across the rubric.
items.assessment: Three concrete authentication-bypass variants are rejected in all five dimensions by local browser assertions. These are not remote LLM shell calibrations; no fresh provider NOP run was made.

items.description: The rubric produces a spread across partial-quality apps, not all-or-nothing.
items.assessment: Current standard continuous60/20/20 reward retained. New scope is unscored by providers. Prior strong GPT result remains0.9595 for r7; no target-band claim.

items.description: Pass/fail behaviors are binary; craft and degree-of-quality are likert with described anchors.
items.assessment: 30 binary criteria and six anchored Visual Likert criteria,36 total. Functional22 plus Render2, Constraints2 and Polish4.

items.description: A worse app never outscores a better one - weights/gates/criteria don't invert the ranking.
items.assessment: All six targeted negative variants fail their intended checkpoints. This establishes local discrimination, not an exhaustive ranking or provider-judge reliability proof.

items.description: Gate/constraint failures hard-zero the quality terms, and passing only the cheap gates earns little.
items.assessment: Authentication is part of each shared zero-credit prerequisite, so a detected access-boundary failure zeros Render/Constraints and the existing total reward formula. The formula itself is unchanged.

items.description: Weight tracks what each thing proves - real functionality is weighted above structure and style.
items.assessment: Dimension weights unchanged60/20/20. Existing Functional weight28 retained plus6 for three distinct new2.0-weight workflows; no duplicate weighting of the seven staff successes.

items.description: Every dimension prompt treats the submission as untrusted and forbids following instructions embedded in it.
items.assessment: All five prompts continue treating submission text as untrusted; they forbid guessed endpoints and copied authenticated credentials in anonymous probes.

items.description: The agent can't read the criteria it's graded on or influence the reward - grading is isolated in the verifier.
items.assessment: Submission UID65534 cannot read tests/config/log directory; verifier-path symlink fails before judge entry.

items.description: Pinned model, temperature 0, versioned prompt, pinned browser, and no unpinned network in the scoring path.
items.assessment: All five changed prompts have incremented plain-Markdown revisions and hashes from the actual verifier image. This removes the specific omission, not remote LLM variance or timing uncertainty.

items.description: Every dimension prompt describes THIS app (credentials, screens, entities, deliverable) with no residue from other work. Reports every instance.
items.assessment: The entire shared gate block is byte-identical across five dimensions. Exact good/bad passwords match the existing Functional check; credential-free protected reads are explicitly allowed in every dimension.

items.block: F - the task as a whole
items.description: Every runtime fact appearing in more than one file (paths, port, seed, accounts, model, weights, literals) agrees everywhere. Reports every drift.
items.assessment: Canonical configuration and runtime checks pass; both seed copies agree; public networking intentional.

items.block: F - the task as a whole
items.description: The directory is the closed list - no scratch, build residue, committed caches, or backups, and all required files present.
items.assessment: 36-task-file allowlist, one named ZIP wrapper; coverage/reports/evidence excluded from upload root.

items.block: F - the task as a whole
items.description: The gating files are well-formed: both TOML families, the shell scripts (bash -n, no CRLF), and the reference/app entry.
items.assessment: TOML/JSON/Python parsed locally; Bash and JavaScript parsed in verifier image; no CRLF shell scripts.

items.block: F - the task as a whole
items.description: No live credentials, real personal data, host paths, unpinned remote fetch, or injection payload anywhere in the task.
items.assessment: No live key literals, personal host paths, real-account data or scoring instructions embedded in seed.

items.block: F - the task as a whole
items.description: The task reads as authored for this product, fits the suite's domain plan, and isn't a nouns-swapped clone of a sibling.
items.assessment: Added multi-step state interactions instead of hidden requirements or copied failure siblings. Captured-model diagnostics are explicitly new-scope observations, not retrospective rescoring.

limits: No provider-backed Oracle, model build or platform static/rubric run on r9.
No guarantee of golden Visual1.0, judge completion time or below0.7 model scores.
Three new requirements were absent from the historical r7 prompt; diagnostics do not change old scores.

user_reported_previous_platform.source: User screenshot, not independently fetched platform data
